author: NorthEast News Desk
body: New Hampshire voters are choosing nominees Tuesday in a primary that will set the field for an open U.S. Senate seat, two congressional contests, the governor’s race and the state Legislature.

The Senate contest has drawn particular attention because Jeanne Shaheen is not seeking reelection. On the Democratic side, U.S. Rep. Chris Pappas is facing a challenge from Karishma Manzur. The Republican field includes former U.S. senators John E. Sununu and Scott Brown.

The ballot also includes a crowded contest for Pappas’s current House seat in the 1st Congressional District. The general election is expected to make New Hampshire one of the country’s closely watched Senate battlegrounds.

The results will provide the first clear measure of which messages, coalitions and candidates have the strongest footing before November. NorthEast News will update this story as results are reported and verified.
dek: Tuesday’s primary is the first major test of the campaigns competing to succeed retiring U.S. Sen. Jeanne Shaheen, with congressional and statehouse contests on the same ballot.
headline: New Hampshire voters head to polls as open Senate seat reshapes 2026 races
